body.statement:
Let \(T\) be a finite set, let \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\) be nonnegative measures on \(T\) having the same total mass \(w\), and let \(Q\subseteq T\times T\).  Put
\[
\Pi(\mu_0,\mu_1)
=\left\{\rho\geq 0:
  \sum_y\rho(x,y)=\mu_0(x),\ 
  \sum_x\rho(x,y)=\mu_1(y)\right\},
\]
\[
N_Q(A)=\{y\in T:\text{there is an }x\in A\text{ with }(x,y)\in Q\},
\qquad
D_Q=\max_{A\subseteq T}\{\mu_0(A)-\mu_1(N_Q(A))\}.
\]
Then
\[
\max_{\rho\in\Pi(\mu_0,\mu_1)}\rho(Q)=w-D_Q.
\]
The maximum is attained.  A capacitated bipartite maximum-flow calculation returns both an attaining coupling and a set \(A\) attaining \(D_Q\).  If \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\) are rational, scaling by a common denominator and using integral augmentations followed by integral residual matching returns a coupling on the same rational lattice.
body.proof_tex:
Construct a directed graph with source \(o\), sink \(t\), a left copy of \(T\), and a right copy of \(T\).  Give \(o\to x\) capacity \(\mu_0(x)\), give \(y\to t\) capacity \(\mu_1(y)\), and give \(x\to y\) capacity \(w+1\) exactly when \((x,y)\in Q\).  The zero flow is feasible, and the finite-dimensional feasible-flow polytope is compact, so a maximum flow \(f\) exists.

Here is a self-contained cut argument.  If the residual graph of \(f\) contained a directed path from \(o\) to \(t\), the minimum residual capacity along that finite path would be positive, and augmenting by this amount would strictly increase the flow.  Thus no such path exists.  Let \(S_f\) be the vertices reachable from \(o\) in the residual graph.  Every original edge leaving \(S_f\) is saturated and every original edge entering \(S_f\) carries zero flow.  Summing flow conservation over the vertices in \(S_f\setminus\{o\}\) therefore shows that the value of \(f\) equals the capacity of the cut \((S_f,S_f^c)\).  Conversely, summing conservation over the source side of any cut shows that every feasible-flow value is at most that cut's capacity.  Hence \(f\) and its residual-reachability cut are respectively a maximum flow and a minimum cut.

The cut that places only \(o\) on the source side has capacity \(w\).  Since every internal edge has capacity \(w+1\), no minimum cut crosses an internal edge.  If \(A\) is the set of left vertices on the source side, every member of \(N_Q(A)\) is consequently on the source side.  Deleting from the source side any right vertex outside \(N_Q(A)\) cannot increase the cut capacity.  Thus a minimum cut has capacity
\[
\min_{A\subseteq T}
\{\mu_0(T\setminus A)+\mu_1(N_Q(A))\}
=w-\max_{A\subseteq T}
\{\mu_0(A)-\mu_1(N_Q(A))\}
=w-D_Q.
\]
The flow on the internal edges is a \(Q\)-supported subcoupling with mass \(w-D_Q\).  Define its residual row and column masses by
\[
r(x)=\mu_0(x)-\sum_y f(x,y),
\qquad
c(y)=\mu_1(y)-\sum_x f(x,y).
\]
Flow conservation gives
\[
\sum_xr(x)=\sum_yc(y)=D_Q.
\]
If \(r(x)>0\), \(c(y)>0\), and \((x,y)\in Q\), then \(o\to x\to y\to t\) is a residual augmenting path: the first and last edges have positive residual capacity, while the internal edge has residual capacity at least \((w+1)-w>0\).  This contradicts maximality.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{supp}(r)\times\operatorname{supp}(c)\subseteq Q^c.
\]
When \(D_Q>0\), set
\[
\rho_Q(x,y)=f(x,y)+\frac{r(x)c(y)}{D_Q};
\]
when \(D_Q=0\), set \(\rho_Q=f\).  In either case \(\rho_Q\in\Pi(\mu_0,\mu_1)\), and the added mass lies in \(Q^c\), so
\[
\rho_Q(Q)=w-D_Q.
\]
For the reverse inequality, for every \(\rho\in\Pi(\mu_0,\mu_1)\) and every \(A\subseteq T\), every \(Q\)-cell either has its left endpoint outside \(A\) or its right endpoint in \(N_Q(A)\).  Hence
\[
\rho(Q)
\leq \mu_0(T\setminus A)+\mu_1(N_Q(A))
=w-\{\mu_0(A)-\mu_1(N_Q(A))\}.
\]
Minimizing the right side over \(A\) proves the claimed equality and attainment.

Finally, suppose a positive integer \(D\) makes \(D\mu_0\) and \(D\mu_1\) integer valued.  After scaling, use internal capacity \(Dw+1\).  Starting from zero, an augmenting-path algorithm always augments by a positive integer.  Its value is bounded by the integer \(Dw\), so it terminates at an integral maximum flow.  The residual row and column masses are integers.  Repeatedly send the smaller of a positive residual row mass and a positive residual column mass between such a pair.  The support argument above ensures that every selected pair lies in \(Q^c\), and each step exhausts a row or a column.  This produces an integral residual matching.  Dividing by \(D\) gives the asserted rational coupling and completes the proof.
